articles.description: Johan Rockström, one of world’s leading climate scientists, says stopping panel from working as quickly as possible is inviting disaster Climate science is “foundational” to the Paris agreement and worldwide progress on tackling global heating, and attempts to delay new scientific reports threaten global cooperation on tackling the crisis, one of the world’s leading climate scientists has warned. Johan Rockström, the director of the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research, said the world’s leading body of climate scientists, the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, must be allowed to work as quickly as possible on its next comprehensive assessment of global knowledge of the climate systems. Continue reading...

articles.title: Could measles and midterms bring down Maha? – podcast

source.name: Presented by Ian Sample, with Jessica Glenza, produced by Ellie Sans, sound design by Joel Cox; the executive producer was Ellie Bury

articles.description: This week the US lost its measles elimination status, an official recognition that the infectious disease is endemic in the country after being eliminated for 26 years. To find out what this means in practical terms for citizens, Ian Sample hears from the Guardian US health reporter Jessica Glenza. She explains why it comes at an already difficult time for the health secretary, Robert F Kennedy Jr, and his Make America Healthy Again movement, and what newly elected Democrats will be focusing on when it comes to health Clips: CBS, NBC, CBC US loses measles elimination status amid worst outbreak since 1991 Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘Remarkable luck’: wreck of first Australian-built warship discovered exactly 128 years after sinking
articles.description: HMCS Spitfire was commissioned by colonial government to protect against Russian warships during the Crimean war The wreck of Australia’s first locally built warship has been discovered 128 years after sinking off the coast of far north Queensland. Marine archaeologists found the remains of Ex HMCS Spitfire on 21 August, the anniversary of its sinking in 1898. Continue reading...

articles.title: Bacterial toxin produced by E coli leading suspect in rise in bowel cancer among under-50s
articles.description: Scientists tell Commons exposure to colibactin in early life is potential driver of early-onset colorectal cancer Exposure to a bacterial toxin in early life has emerged as a leading suspect in the rise of bowel cancer among those under 50, MPs have heard. Cases of early-onset bowel cancer have doubled in many countries in the past two decades, and while rising obesity and a fall in physical activity are contributors, researchers believe other factors must also be involved. Continue reading...

articles.title: Nasa’s Voyager 1 just reached a massive milestone in space - video

source.name: Presented by Madeleine Finlay , produced by Madeleine Finlay and Joshan Chana , graphics by Natalie Gegan

articles.description: Nasa sent the Voyager 1 and 2 probes into space almost 50 years ago to explore the outer reaches of our solar system. Now Voyager 1, the farthest human-made object from Earth, is about to reach a distance of one light-day away from our planet. To find out more about its astonishing journey, Madeleine Finlay hears from Jim Bell, a planetary scientist and professor at Arizona State University’s school of Earth and space exploration. He explains the seismic impact the mission has had on our understanding of the solar system, and where Voyager 1 could be heading now it has left the heliosphere Continue reading...

articles.title: After 49 years, Nasa’s Voyager 1 is one light-day away from us. Can we save this ‘pale blue dot’? | Kim Heacox
articles.description: Since the spacecraft’s 1977 launch, our wonderful and terrible species has done great damage to our planet. Voyager has offered us a clear view of ourselves Imagine traveling nonstop for 49 years, alone in the dark with no destination in sight, powered by curiosity and engineering. Further imagine making that journey not at bullet train or jet plane speed, but much faster: at 37,800 miles per hour, free from friction in a vast sea of cold, soundless space, bombarded by radiation and cosmic rays yet still able to communicate with folks back home. Continue reading...

articles.title: Pill that mimics Viagra can slow Alzheimer’s progression, study suggests
articles.description: Experts call trial results of medication that slowed cognitive decline by almost a third ‘very promising’ A pill that mimics Viagra by relaxing blood vessels and increasing blood flow to the brain can slow cognitive decline in people with Alzheimer’s disease by almost a third, a global study suggests. Alzheimer’s is the most common form of dementia, a condition that is forecast to affect 153 million people worldwide by 2050. There is currently no cure. Continue reading...

articles.title: Senate committee rejects Trump nominee to lead National Science Foundation
articles.description: Committee chair Bill Cassidy, a Republican, said Jim O’Neill ‘did not do enough to stand up for science’ in previous posts Jim O’Neill will not undergo a confirmation hearing on Wednesday to head he National Science Foundation (NSF) because he “did not do enough to stand up for science” in his previous position, said Bill Cassidy, a Republican from Louisiana who is chair of the Senate committee on health, education, labor and pensions. This ends O’Neill’s run for the top US scientific organization, an embattled independent federal agency that has seen major budget cuts and grant freezes under the Trump administration. The next NSF nominee will face a Democratic-led Senate. Continue reading...
